title: Flash Sale / Ticketing
summary: A flash sale sends a million people at 10,000 items in the same second. The system cannot serve everyone at once, and it must never sell item 10,001. So it protects itself in layers. A CDN absorbs page loads and bots, a virtual waiting room admits buyers at a rate the backend can handle, and stock is decremented atomically so each unit is held by exactly one buyer until they pay or the hold expires.

walkthrough.title: Crowd arrives
walkthrough.text: At 10:00:00 a million users load the sale page. It is static and served from CDN cache, while bot detection and per-IP limits drop scripted traffic at the edge.

walkthrough.title: Join the waiting room
walkthrough.text: Users get a queue position. Randomising positions among those who arrived before the start removes the advantage of refreshing fastest.

walkthrough.title: Admit at a safe rate
walkthrough.text: The waiting room lets in, say, 2,000 users per second, a rate the backend was load-tested for, and gives each one a signed, short-lived admission token.

walkthrough.title: Request a reservation
walkthrough.text: The admitted user clicks Buy. The reservation service rejects any request without a valid token, so skipping the queue does not work.

walkthrough.title: Atomically take one unit
walkthrough.text: A Lua script in Redis checks stock > 0 and decrements it in one atomic step. Two buyers can never both get the last unit, and the database is not involved yet.

walkthrough.title: Hold and pay
walkthrough.text: A hold with a 10-minute expiry is written and an order is queued. The user pays within the hold window, and the order is confirmed asynchronously.

walkthrough.title: Release expired holds
walkthrough.text: Unpaid holds expire and their units go back into stock, so the next people admitted from the queue can buy them.

data.label: Buyers

output.name: Actions
output.type: Load page · join queue · reserve · pay

responsibilities: Load the event page and wait in line.
Complete payment before the hold expires.
Keep the queue tab open; no refreshing needed.

failureModes.impact: Load multiplies; users lose their place.
failureModes.mitigation: Queue position bound to a cookie and token; refresh resumes the same spot.
Bot scoring, verified accounts, purchase limits per account and card.

data.label: CDN & Bot Defence

input.name: Requests
input.type: Millions of page loads and API calls per second

output.name: Filtered
output.type: Cached pages served; legitimate API calls passed through

responsibilities: Serves the sale page and assets from cache so origins see none of it.
Blocks bots and enforces per-IP and per-account rate limits.
Routes queue and reservation calls to the right services.

failureModes.impact: The origin is hit with millions of page loads.
failureModes.mitigation: Fully static page; personal data fetched by a small API call later.
Layered signals (device, behaviour, account age), not CAPTCHA alone.

data.label: Virtual Waiting Room

output.name: Admission
output.type: Position, then token { eventId, user, exp: 10 min }

responsibilities: Turns a spike into a steady flow the backend can handle.
Admits users in order at a configurable rate.
Issues tokens that are verified without a database lookup.

failureModes.impact: Backend overloads and everyone gets errors.
failureModes.mitigation: Set from load tests; adjust automatically on backend latency.
Bind the token to session and account; single-use for reserve.

data.label: Reservation Service
responsibilities: Validates admission token, purchase limits, and idempotency.
Decrements stock atomically before anything slower happens.
Answers 'sold out' instantly once stock hits zero.

failureModes.impact: Race between buyers, so the item is oversold.
failureModes.mitigation: Single atomic operation (Lua / DECR with check, or a conditional DB update).

failureModes.scenario: Client retries a reserve that succeeded
failureModes.impact: Two units held for one buyer.
failureModes.mitigation: Idempotency key per user and SKU.

data.label: Stock Counter
responsibilities: Holds available units in memory for fast atomic decrements.
Is loaded from the database before the sale starts.
Gets units back when holds expire or orders are cancelled.

failureModes.scenario: One SKU key is the hottest key in the system
failureModes.mitigation: Split stock into N sub-counters across shards; try another when one hits zero.

failureModes.impact: Counter is higher than reality, so units are oversold.
failureModes.mitigation: Reconcile against durable holds before confirming; keep a small unsold buffer.

data.label: Holds & Order Queue

output.name: Order
output.type: Order created once payment succeeds; expiries release stock

responsibilities: Records each hold durably, the real source of truth for who got a unit.
Queues order creation so the database writes at a steady pace.
Expires unpaid holds and returns their units.

failureModes.impact: Units stuck in dead holds; the event shows sold out too early.
failureModes.mitigation: Expiry by timestamp checked on read, plus a frequent sweeper.

failureModes.scenario: Payment completes just after the hold expired
failureModes.impact: Charged but the unit was released to someone else.
failureModes.mitigation: Grace period, and a conditional confirm that refunds if the hold is gone.

data.label: Payment Provider
responsibilities: Charges the buyer during the hold window.
Reports results asynchronously by webhook.
Absorbs payment spikes within its own rate limits.

failureModes.impact: Payments fail and holds expire unpaid.
failureModes.mitigation: Pre-arranged capacity with the provider; pace admissions to payment throughput too.

failureModes.impact: Order not confirmed though the user paid.
failureModes.mitigation: Poll the payment status before expiring a hold that has a payment attempt.
